source: Wizards of the Coast's Commander Brackets as the app has carried them since the lobby's BRACKETS table (crankmagic-lobby.js) and the Lab's compliance tiers (compliance-model.js) were written from the published system; the Game Changer list is the card record's gameChanger flag (Scryfall's game_changer, refreshed with the record set). When Wizards revises the system, this file's updatedAt moves with it and the report says which date it judged by.

rules.label: Game Changers
rules.says: Cards on Wizards' Game Changer list: the ones that most warp a casual table.

rules.label: Mass land denial
rules.says: Destroying, sacrificing or locking down everyone's lands at once.

rules.label: Chained extra turns
rules.says: Extra turns taken in a row, or an extra-turn spell that comes back to be cast again.

rules.label: Two-card infinite combos
rules.says: Two cards that together win or lock the game on the spot.

rules.label: Tutors
rules.says: Cards that search the library for exactly what the deck wants; not a rule, a texture the lower brackets keep light.

brackets.name: Exhibition
brackets.says: Ultra-casual. No Game Changers, no mass land denial, no chained extra turns, no two-card infinite combos. Winning is not the point.

brackets.name: Core
brackets.says: Precon level. No Game Changers, and the same three restrictions. Games run long and end on a big turn.

brackets.name: Upgraded
brackets.says: Up to three Game Changers. No mass land denial, no chained extra turns, and a two-card combo only as a late-game finish.

brackets.name: Optimized
brackets.says: No restrictions. The strongest build of whatever the deck wants to do.

brackets.name: cEDH
brackets.says: No restrictions, and every seat is playing to win as fast as the format allows.
